- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–8% from forecast for next 7–10 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–7) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply a 1–4% downward bias to first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values, model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizon; if forecast is > 20% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% for next 7–10 days.
- When sentiment spikes to 1.0, model often overreacts; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak, then apply 2–5% decay per day for next 5–7 days.
